title: 3 Stocks in a Bull Rally Right Now
author: Tracey Ryniec
description: While AI stocks face uncertainty following NVIDIA CEO's resignation, several non-technology companies are breaking out to new highs with strong earnings. Visa beat earnings again with 21.4% YTD gains and raised its dividend 16%. Ralph Lauren reported strong full-price demand and raised FY2027 guidance with 10.3% YTD gains. Eli Lilly surged 23% in one month on 39% revenue growth driven by GLP-1 products Mounjaro and Zepbound, raising full-year earnings guidance.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Consistent earnings beats since 2008 IPO, strong payment and cross-border volume growth, 16% dividend increase, 21.4% YTD gains at new all-time highs, and expected 13.2% earnings growth in FY2027 with reasonable forward P/E of 28.

Beat consensus estimates, strong full-price demand across all regions led by Asia, successful US Open collection, raised FY2027 guidance, expected 12.8% earnings growth, and Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating despite being near all-time highs.

Beat consensus estimates, 39% Q3 revenue growth from GLP-1 products (Mounjaro and Zepbound), raised full-year earnings guidance, 23% surge in one month, 46.1% expected earnings growth in 2026, and trillion-dollar market cap status despite elevated forward P/E of 40.

title: Zacks.com featured highlights include Ralph Lauren, Expedia, NVIDIA and Lam Research
author: Zacks.Com
description: Zacks.com highlights four GARP (Growth at a Reasonable Price) stocks as attractive investment opportunities: Ralph Lauren, Expedia Group, NVIDIA, and Lam Research. These stocks combine value and growth metrics, offering solid earnings prospects with reasonable valuations. All four companies have raised guidance, demonstrated strong earnings surprises, and maintain positive momentum in their respective sectors.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Raised fiscal 2027 guidance with 6-7% constant-currency revenue growth, operating margin expansion of 80-100 basis points, inventory down 9% YoY, completed $500M buyback, and maintained $1 quarterly dividend. Zacks Rank #2 with consistent earnings beat history (8.44% average surprise).

Raised full-year 2026 guidance with gross bookings of $131.4-$131.9B and EBITDA margin expansion of 1.8-2 points. Strong product momentum with 30+ new features released. Zacks Rank #1 with consistent earnings beats (15.26% average surprise) and $0.48 quarterly dividend.

Projects Q3 fiscal 2027 revenues of $108B with 74% gross margin. Strong product ramps (Vera Rubin in full production) and $150B added to buyback authorization. Zacks Rank #2 with consistent earnings beats (5.82% average surprise), though leadership transition presents some uncertainty.

December-quarter guidance of $8.6B revenues with 52.5% non-GAAP gross margin. Strong demand linked to AI-driven device complexity, new logistics hub for operational efficiency, and $25B repurchase authorization. Zacks Rank #2 with consistent earnings beats (6.43% average surprise) and $0.33 quarterly dividend.

title: Ralph Lauren: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
author: The Motley Fool Team
description: Ralph Lauren reported strong Q2 earnings with revenue growth of 28% in Asia and over 35% in China, driven by direct-to-consumer sales. The company raised full-year guidance, boosted margins through 9% average unit retail price increases, and is strategically exiting lower-tier retail channels to protect its premium brand positioning. Management plans to maintain high marketing investments while navigating traffic headwinds in Europe.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong Q2 results with 28% Asia revenue growth, 35% China growth, 9% AUR increase, raised full-year guidance, improved margins to 70%, and successful execution of premium brand strategy. The company demonstrated pricing power and added 1.7 million new direct customers, indicating solid business momentum despite some European traffic headwinds.

title: G-III's DTC Strategy Gains Traction as DKNY & Donna Karan Grow Online
author: Zacks.Com
description: G-III Apparel Group is successfully building its direct-to-consumer business around owned brands as Calvin Klein and Tommy Hilfiger licenses wind down. DKNY's online sales grew mid-20% year-over-year with improved conversion and pricing, while Donna Karan brand sales surged over 45%. The Marc Jacobs acquisition, which closed September 1st, adds over 100 stores and an established e-commerce platform. G-III raised fiscal 2027 adjusted EPS guidance to $2.20-$2.30 and sees potential for Marc Jacobs to generate $1 billion in annual revenues long-term.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong DTC momentum with DKNY online sales growing mid-20%, Donna Karan surging 45%, Marc Jacobs acquisition adding significant retail footprint, and raised fiscal 2027 EPS guidance. Company is successfully transitioning away from winding-down licenses to owned brands with healthy full-price selling and improving metrics.
